disposition_reason: The current original findings estimate ripple-rate learning effects and ripple/grid/behavior associations. Their coefficients and p-values are not performance measures that can be improved by exceeding the reported value. Turning these into a new decoder or detector would change the task.

source_paper.title: Human hippocampal ripples align new experiences with a grid-like schema

evidence.locator: Summary; Results: Task and intracranial recordings, Hippocampal ripple activity increases as learning progresses; Fig. 4G,H
evidence.supports: The study reports learning-related ripple effects and associations between rest ripples, grid modulation and inference; these are scientific estimands, not a benchmarked prediction algorithm.
Loads processed learning rates, excludes phase-specific upper 1% of positive ripple values, fits phase/accuracy/trial mixed models, and relates subject-level Learn-R to behavior.

evidence.locator: Grid coefficient summaries and partial-correlation analysis; Fig. 4 plotting blocks
evidence.supports: The script uses already estimated grid coefficients and reports association/correlation results. The filename does not establish out-of-sample predictive accuracy.

evidence.locator: Version v2, published August 27 2025; description and file inventory
evidence.supports: Released processed neural/behavioral data; large HFB and contact files are on Zenodo and smaller complementary files are in the author repository.

target.description: Estimate learning-phase and accuracy effects on hippocampal ripple rates and their association with inference, HFB and estimated grid modulation. These observational effects have no source-defined direction that an alternative algorithm should maximize.

dataset.description: Processed author data in Zenodo v2 record 16950716 plus the pinned repository tables; no raw-sEEG detector benchmark is supplied by this release.

cohort.description: The source recruited 42 epilepsy patients, retained 38 for analysis, and reports 181 hippocampal contacts in 34 subjects. Analysis-specific contact availability must remain explicit rather than treating every contact as an independent patient.

split.description: The registered rate/behavior association endpoint is inferential, without a held-out predictive-performance target. The paper's grid-orientation cross-validation supports estimating grid modulation, not optimizing the learning-rate association or scoring the supplied coefficient table as a decoder.

inputs.description: Trial/phase ripple rates, subject/channel identifiers, trial accuracy and behavior summaries; additional HFB and estimated grid coefficients support the corresponding association analyses.

preprocessing.description: Author learning script removes values above each phase's 99th percentile of positive ripple rates, reshapes phase rates and selects correct trials for Learn-R, with explicit outlier removal and channel-to-subject averaging.

metric.description: Mixed-model coefficients, covariance, Learn-R, partial correlations and their uncertainty are estimates to reproduce or challenge. A larger positive slope, correlation or smaller p-value is not a scientifically ordered performance improvement.

aggregation.description: The Learn-R route computes channel/phase estimates then averages to subject level before behavior association. Preserve source model grouping and per-analysis support; do not aggregate contacts as independent subjects.

comparison.primary_metric: No eligible ordered performance metric for the registered ripple-rate and grid-association findings

published_baseline.description: Reported effects and correlations are not algorithm-performance baselines to exceed.

reproduced_author_baseline.description: A faithful mixed-model or coefficient-table reconstruction is calibration, not a baseline whose scientific value increases when exceeded.

minimum_effect.rationale: There is no meaningful positive performance margin for increasing a biological association estimate.

uncertainty.method: Source association uncertainty may be reproduced, but no performance-difference test is defined.
uncertainty.independent_unit: Patient, with contacts nested within patient.
uncertainty.rationale: Stronger statistical significance would not improve the source finding; changing the estimand would require a separately registered scientific task.

paper_win_requires: No active same-task paper win is admitted for these descriptive endpoints.
Retain source effects, nulls and uncertainty without rewarding their magnitude or significance.

Any proposed held-patient behavior decoder, raw ripple detector or re-estimated grid-orientation benchmark needs its own source-backed original task and baseline; it cannot retroactively replace this task.

current_sota.description: No current-SOTA comparison was verified; source-paper results and any future author rerun remain separate comparators.

episode.improvement_loop: Inactive for this ineligible descriptive task. Existing fitting/reconstruction can assess computational calibration only.
episode.candidate_freeze: For any retained calibration run, freeze the source estimand, inclusion and fitting choices before comparing reference estimates; this does not create a performance episode.
episode.final_evaluation: Report reconstruction fidelity and scientific sensitivity separately, with no stronger-than-paper reward.
episode.baseline_policy: Neither reference coefficient agreement nor a larger effect/smaller p-value is source-paper improvement. No author predictive-performance baseline was identified.

blocking_issues: The registered scientific target is a descriptive association with no defensible ordered performance endpoint.
Raw-sEEG ripple detection and fresh grid estimation are outside the demonstrated processed inputs.
A different supervised decoder would require a distinct source-grounded task; it is not a repair by changing this task's success metric.

legacy.notes: Preserve registered-runtime/program-v1/portable/task and score.py. Their reconstruction of three learning-phase mixed models, preprocessing support and covariance is calibration only; the task itself states there is no reward for a positive slope or small p-value.
